title: Base-flat modules on localized open sites
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq X$ an open, and $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] affine-locally flat over $f$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Restrict $G$ to the localized site over $U$ and restrict scalars along the canonical map $(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S)|_U\to\mathcal O_X|_U$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. The resulting sheaf is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] over $(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S)|_U$. Neither quasi-coherence nor a nonempty open is assumed.

source.place: Tags 01U2 (section-flat), 05NE (stalk criterion) and 0098 (stalks of pullbacks); open-site restriction of the relative_flat_module_stalk calculation

proof.text: Apply isFlat_open_scalarRestriction_of_stalks to the inverse-image ring and tensorPullbackRingMap. At x in U use exists_inverseImageStructure_stalk_iso to obtain a base-to-inverse-image stalk ring isomorphism compatible with the structure map.

Apply relative_flat_module_stalk with the algebra defined by f.stalkMap x. Restrict the inverse-image ring action via the inverse of the stalk isomorphism. The compatibility equation proves the scalar-tower law. A bijective ring map is flat; transitivity of module flatness then proves the stalk hypothesis of the open-site criterion.

lean.statement:
theorem relativeFlat_open_scalarRestriction
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (U : X.Opens) (G : X.Modules)
    (hflat : G.IsFlatOver f) :
    let α := ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).overPullback CommRingCat.{u} U).map
      (Modules.tensorPullbackRingMap f)
    let B := (sheafCompose ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).over U)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map α
    SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars B).obj
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).obj G))
